newsitem.title: UK: S&P watching Deutsche, focus on control.
newsitem.headline: S&P watching Deutsche, focus on control.

text.p: Standard & Poor's plans to monitor developments at Deutsche Bank but has taken no rating actions on the German bank, an S&P director said on Monday.

S&P director Barry Hancock told Reuters the agency would be meeting with Deutsche Bank in the normal course of business to discuss recent events and was most interested in examining issues about internal controls at the bank.
"As events emerge we'll obviously be following them and be having meetings with management," Hancock said. "The control issues are the ones which will be higher up the agenda."

Deutsche Bank, one of the few banks left in the world to carry triple-A ratings from both Moody's Investors Service and S&P, has been in the spotlight due to problems at its Morgan Grenfell Asset Management (MGAM) fund management arm.
Deutsche has had to inject capital into MGAM, which has suffered an exodus of investors following a temporary suspension of three of its funds recently due to "irregularities".

Hancock's remarks follow comments from a Moody's banking analyst last week who said Moody's was looking at the implications of the MGAM situation regarding Deutsche's rating. Moody's current outlook on Deutsche's rating is negative.
But Hancock said the troubles at Deutsche were not big enough to warrant an immediate change in its rating.
"Clearly when you have a group of the size and weight of capital of Deutsche it can get through these sorts of things without a knock on the rating," he said.

The manager of two MGAM funds, Peter Young, has been suspended and his assets frozen pending a probe into the management of the trusts, which held a high proportion of unlisted, high technology stocks.
Deutsche last week took those stocks into its books in return for a 180 million stg cash injection into MGAM and has pledged further backing if necessary.
